Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT DILG-NAPOLCOM Center, EDSA cor. Quezon Avenue, West Triangle, Quezon City dilq qov.ph DILG OPINION No. 11 s. 2023 MAR 10 2023 HON. JUAN FERNANDO LARONG Sangguniang Panlalawigan Member Surigao del Norte Dear SP Member Larong: This has reference to your letter dated January 16, 2023 requesting for this Department's opinion on the following: I. 2. Whether the sand and gravel and other quarry resources coming from sources outside Surigao del Norte, being finished products already are considered goods or merchandise within the contemplation of DILG-ARTA- DOF Joint Memorandum Circular No. 2021-01; Whether Section 100 of Provincial Tax Ordinance No. 01, s.2020, the Revenue Code of 2019 of the Province of Surigao del Norte should be amended/suspended/repealed for being violative of DILG-ARTA-DOF Joint Memorandum Circular No. 2021-01 and/or Section 133 of the Local Govemment Code of 1991. Per your representation, the monopoly of sand and gravel in Siargao Island, Surigao del Norte led to severe shortage on sand and gravel supplies. This has adverse effects on govemment infrastructure projects and have already caused most govemment projects to be suspended. The provincial govemments strict implementation of the subject ordinance has caused extreme backlash and criticism on the legislative department of the provincial govemment. Section 100 of the subject ordinance provides: Section 100. Sand and Gravel and Other Quarry Resources coming from Surigao outside del Norte. The sources quarry operator/permittee/contractor/truck driver shall carry and produce the following requirements before allowed entry and delivery of sand, gravel, earth and other quarry materials to any destination within the province. 1. Presentation of approved Governors Permit with proof of payment for materials quarried/extracted from other provinces; 2. Delivery receipt specifying the kind of materials and carried load and "Matino, Mahusay at Maaasahan" Trunkline No.: 8876-34-54

With respect to the second issue, we also answer in the affirrnative, such provision should be amended/repealed accordingly pursuant to Item 4.2 of the DILG-ARTA-DOF Joint Memorandum Circular No. 2021-01 and Item 3.1.2 of DILG Memorandum Circular No. 2021-01 , viz: 4.2. All policies, issuances, ordinance, or resolutions inconsistent with this JMC shall be subject to repeal or amendment consistent with DILG- ARTA Joint Memorandum Circular 2019-01 dated December 11 , 2019, entitled "Guidelines on the Regulatory Reform for LGUs in Pursuant to the Ease of Doing Business and Efficient Govemment Service Delivery Act of 2018". 3.1.2. Cause the immediate repeal ofthe ordinance imposing the above-cited fees and taxes Be that as it may, please be informed that the Department has already issued several policies on the imposition and collection of pass-through fees being imposed by local govemment units. As early as 26 June 2006, Memorandum Circular No. 2006-70 was issued on the suspension of LGU imposition and collection of illegal fees and taxes pursuant to Section 133 (3) of the LGC. This was followed by a reiteration memorandum, through Memorandum Circular No. 2009-42 which serve as a guide and reminder to the public officers of LGUs in the imposition and collection of local taxes, fees and charges. More recently, amid reports that some local govemment units are still imposing the pass-through fees despite previous directives enjoining them to discontinue the imposition and collection of such fees and taxes, Memorandum Circular No- 2018-133 was issued enjoining local chief executives to "refrain from enforcing any existing ordinance authorizing the levy of fees and taxes on inter-province transport of goods, regulatory fees in local ports, and other additional taxes, fees or charges in any form upon transporting goods or merchandise. It also directed local chief executives to immediately repeal of any ordinance imposing the above cited fees and taxes. Please be guided accordingly. Very truly yours, AUTH RITY OF THE SECRETARY: AN VI TOR R. LLAMAS Un e ecretary for Extemal, Legal and Legislative Affairs LL RPB/LRALLD/rrao copy furnished: DIR LILIBETH A.
